categories.name: Sign Reversal / Transposition Error
categories.description: Failure to invert signs when transposing terms across the equality operator, or erroneous negative multiplication.
categories.misconceptionExplanation: Student treats the equals sign as an inert separator rather than a balance operator, forgetting that adding or subtracting across sides inverts the term's sign.
categories.remedialAction: Provide balancing beam visualization and step-by-step subtraction/addition demonstration on both sides simultaneously.

categories.name: Partial Distribution Error
categories.description: Multiplying the factor outside parentheses by only the first term inside parentheses.
categories.misconceptionExplanation: Student forgets that a multiplier outside parentheses applies to every monomial term enclosed within parentheses: a(b + c) = ab + ac, not ab + c.
categories.remedialAction: Highlight grouped terms with area-model expansion boxes before algebraic substitution.

categories.name: Incompatible Variable Combination
categories.description: Adding or subtracting coefficient of variable with a constant term (e.g., 3x + 4 = 7x).
categories.misconceptionExplanation: Student conflates algebraic variables with scalar constants, ignoring dimensional/term compatibility.
categories.remedialAction: Use tactile counters or fruit metaphors (apples vs oranges) to reinforce that variables cannot merge with scalar numbers.

categories.name: Denominator Clearance / LCM Omission
categories.description: Multiplying only one side or a subset of terms by the common denominator when clearing fractions.
categories.misconceptionExplanation: Student forgets that maintaining equation equivalence requires distributing the LCM across all additive terms on both sides of the equation.
categories.remedialAction: Require explicit parentheses around entire left and right hand expressions before applying multiplier.

categories.name: Basic Calculation Slip
categories.description: Elementary multiplication, division, addition, or subtraction mistake during intermediate evaluation.
categories.misconceptionExplanation: Conceptual understanding of algebra is intact, but working memory cognitive overload caused an arithmetic execution mistake.
categories.remedialAction: Isolate the arithmetic operation into a scratch step to decouple algorithmic strategy from computation.
